title: Bound every finite autonomous device under an admitted depolarizing perturbation
statement: Add E=(epsilon/2)sum_v(T_v-id) with eta=epsilon/2; each complete-site term has diamond norm<=epsilon and the total remains GKLS. During tau=1/(2Jn), all n sites have at least one independent replacement with probability p_n=(1-exp(-eta tau))^n. Suppressing nominal evolution on such a clock history yields the global replacement channel; telescoping costs<=tau||L0||diamond<=1/2. Therefore traceless-Hermitian inputs contract by<=1-p_n/2 per interval and by<=exp(-k p_n/2) after k. For ANY encoder A and decoder B, ||B exp(k tau K)A-id_2||diamond>=1-exp(-k p_n/2), witnessed already by two logical basis inputs. Since p_n>=(eta/(4Jn))^n, fixed nonzero loss occurs by exp[O(n log(n/epsilon))] time. All device sites and nominal controllers are included. This ceiling is compatible with some stretched-exponential lifetimes at polynomial hardware size and is not the requested full-model no-go.

assumptions: The central non-equilibrium unsafe-occupation bound must hold for the COMPLETE paid perturbed generator; equilibrium Peierls suppression does not establish it. Added depolarization generally destroys Gibbs stationarity even at zero perturbation. Imported passive-memory and asynchronous-classical comparisons retain only their supplied stated scopes; no new original-body acquisition or generic thermal-to-arbitrary-GKLS transfer. No positive full threshold/no-go or new independent Capital audit. CONTINUATION: The full model permits this particular depolarizing perturbation, so the bound is genuinely model-wide for finite devices, but exp[O(n log(n/epsilon))] can exceed the desired exp(cL^a) for polynomial n(L). It therefore does not refute the target. Existing asynchronous/classical/CSS/thermal premises retain their scoped hypotheses; paid CP clocks do not establish bounded semantic damage or quantum fault containment. Robust unsafe occupation and noisy native encoded boundaries remain unconstructed. Root35–45 assessment applies to22C, not automatically to this new5C5 proof.
costs: Adversarial perturbation uses actual complete-site replacement clocks eta=epsilon/2. Use tau=1/(2Jn),p_n=(1-exp(-eta tau))^n. Bounds charge the complete generator norm and every site; constants depend only on fixed local strength. This is an analytic upper bound, not an implemented or efficient correction device. No scientific code run or primary-source recovery.
